title: Mexico Faces Colombia Under New Rafael Márquez Leadership
seoTitle: Mexico Faces Colombia Under New Rafael Márquez Leadership
subtitle: 2026 Friendly Marks Rafael Márquez's First Match as Mexico National Team Coach
excerpt: Rafael Márquez debuts as Mexico's national team coach in a friendly against Colombia at M&T Bank Stadium in Baltimore, with free-to-air TV broadcast.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Rafael Márquez takes the helm of the Mexican national team, with his first match scheduled against Colombia in a friendly as part of the preparation for the 2026 World Cup. The clash, taking place at M&T Bank Stadium in Baltimore, United States, has generated significant interest among fans and sports analysts.

Márquez's First Statement on Playing Style

Before the match, the coach explained that he does not intend to automatically transfer Barcelona's style to the national team. He emphasized that, although he was developed at the Catalan club, the Mexican team does not possess the “raw material” needed to replicate the football of that period. Márquez highlighted the necessity of adapting concepts to the profile of the available players and gradually building their own identity.

Match Details: Mexico vs. Colombia

The friendly will be played on Saturday, September 26, starting at 7 PM (Mexico City time), at M&T Bank Stadium in Baltimore, Maryland. The match is part of the preparation schedule for the 2026 World Cup and serves as the first practical test of the new coach's ideas.

How to Watch the Game Live

The broadcast will be free on Canal 5, Televisa's open signal, and will also be available on pay channels that offer TUDN programming. Furthermore, the match can be followed on digital platforms such as ViX and TUDN En Vivo, which allow access via mobile devices, computers, tablets, and smart TVs. Mexican fans residing in the United States can tune into TUDN USA's coverage through local cable TV providers.

Expectations for the National Team's Performance

Márquez indicated that his initial focus will be to continue concepts already demonstrated by the team during the last World Cup, progressively introducing new ideas as the players develop. He acknowledged the short timeframe to work with the squad, comparing the process to “planting a seed”.

Impact of the Friendly on 2026 Preparation

The encounter against Colombia offers the coach an opportunity to evaluate the individual quality and the players' ability to interpret spaces, aspects he deemed essential for implementing a more technical playing style. The result and collective performance will serve as a reference for tactical adjustments in future call-ups heading towards the next World Cup.

With information from OneFootball, Depor.
